evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Chinese Etymology)
evidence.field: 形義源流通解; graphic history
evidence.text: The entry says 后 appears in bronze inscriptions by the late Spring and Autumn period with the sense ‘ruler.’ It reports that 后 and 司 are distinguished by orientation in bronze forms, while oracle-bone forms do not distinguish direction; it attributes the same-graph interpretation to Tang Lan and Li Xiaoding. It separately reports Wang Guowei’s identification of an oracle form of 后 written with 毓. These are competing accounts; the entry does not establish a graphic sequence or settled decomposition.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：后

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 (Taiwan Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants)
evidence.field: 研訂說明; loan and standardization history
evidence.text: The opened entry says 后 and 後 were originally distinct graphs with the same sound and were substituted for one another in texts. It cites the received Yili 大射 passage and Liji 大學 知止而后有定 as uses of 后 for 後, then notes similar usage in Song–Yuan and later popular texts. It says mainland simplified-character tables issued in 1964 and 1986 explicitly used 后 as the simplified form of 後. This supports an attested spelling loan and later standardization; it does not establish the words’ ancient pronunciation beyond the dictionary’s same-sound account.
evidence.title: [A01287-012] 后 (後) - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》
evidence.field: 釋義; cited examples for 后
evidence.text: The entry gives Mandarin hòu and separately records ‘king,’ ‘feudal lord,’ and ‘ruler’s principal wife,’ citing Shijing 商頌·玄鳥, Zuozhuan 僖公三十二年, Shujing 舜典, and Han shu 景帝紀. It also records 后 for ‘later’ as 通後, citing Liji 大學. These are received-text examples and the entry does not date transitions among senses.
evidence.title: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》：后

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Chinese Etymology)
evidence.field: 《說文》; 《廣韻》; Mandarin and Middle Chinese readings
evidence.text: The entry reproduces Shuowen’s ‘successor ruler’ definition and its account of a human figure issuing commands, analyzed with 一 and 口. It lists Guangyun fanqie 胡口 and 胡遘, with Middle Chinese categories 匣母侯韻, upper and departing tones. These document the historical lexicographic account and readings, not proof that Shuowen’s graphic analysis is correct.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：后

evidence.text: The Commons file page describes the image as a Shuowen Jiezi radical in Lesser Seal script, identifies it as uploader LiliCharlie’s own work, dated 9 December 2013, and specifies CC BY-SA 3.0 with attribution and share-alike requirements. This is a modern redrawn seal-script image, not an early inscription specimen; no graphic pixels were inspected here, and the candidate does not resolve 后’s disputed early form.

evidence.field: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv exact rows; Baxter–Sagart Mandarin/MC/OC table
evidence.text: The supplied exact Baxter–Sagart rows give 后: MC huwX, OC *ɢˤ(r)oʔ, gloss ‘sovereign; queen’; 後: MC huwX, OC *[ɢ]ˤ(r)oʔ, gloss ‘after’, plus MC huwH, OC *[ɢ]ˤ(r)oʔ-s, ‘put after ?’; 口: MC khuwX, OC *kʰˤ(r)oʔ, ‘mouth’. Thus 后 and 後 share listed MC but their OC entries differ in the bracketed initial notation, which must not be silently harmonized; 口 has a different reconstructed reading and provides no phonetic support for 后. These readings do not establish the origin of either graph. The upstream PDF search result exposed the 口 row, but opening it failed.

gaps: The early graphic origin of 后 remains unsettled. Sources report both the 后/司 same-graph or orientation account and Wang Guowei’s report of an oracle form written with 毓; neither establishes a complete sequence into the received graph, and no corruption path is demonstrated.

A late Spring and Autumn bronze attestation for 后 with the sense ‘ruler’ is reported by CUHK, but primary inscription editions and the date/identity of earlier oracle uses were not independently verified here. The reported earliest bronze date should not be treated as secure proof that all visually similar oracle forms are the same graph or lexeme.

The dossier’s childbirth-to-succession-to-empress account and rear-body/anus account are not demonstrated by the inspected paleographic evidence. Received-text ruler, lord, and ruler’s-wife citations establish uses, not a dated semantic chain.

The classical spelling loan后 for 後 is now supported by an opened Ministry dictionary entry citing Yili and Liji examples. The exact chronology and circumstances of its first use remain undated; modern standardization is reported as occurring in 1964 and 1986.

For phonology, the supplied local rows show Baxter–Sagart 2014 MC huwX for 后 and 後 but different OC notation (*ɢˤ(r)oʔ vs *[ɢ]ˤ(r)oʔ); the source PDF could not be opened for direct upstream verification. Unihan character-specific pages for 后, 後, and 口 were inaccessible, so the supplied local kMandarin readings are not externally confirmed in this session.

The ordinary 后-seal Commons page failed to open, its exact image pixels and metadata could not be verified, and the MediaWiki imageinfo API attempt was inaccessible through the browser. The Shuowen radical 335 Commons candidate is a modern redrawn seal form with CC BY-SA 3.0 terms, not an early inscription; it was not selected as an illustration of disputed origin.
No tracked extract is recommended: the inspected sources are character-specific dictionary records or individual image records, and no broad reuse permission for dictionary content was established.
